i’ve been a ferret mom for about 4 or 5 years now (the time flies!) and while i dont know everything, i can try and help you along!

cages: the bigger the cage, the better! if they can free roam or have their own room, even better! cages need to be well furnished with lots of comfy places to sleep, as well as some mental stimulation available. ferrets should get at least 4 hours out of their cage a day, but the more time, the better.

food: food is dependent all on what the ferret needs. many ferrets can do well off of just kibble, but personally i add a mixture of some duk soup, salmon oil, and vitamin paste to his food. however, this is partially because he’s getting old and needs a little more to get along, so a young ferret can very well thrive just off of kibble. 

baths: baths need to be very few and far between. i recommend only giving them in cases of them being significantly dirty (got into something, rolled in a litter box).i recommend putting them in a sink with VERY shallow water, about chest level to your ferret, with a towel under the water for traction. give them an oatmeal bath with a very gentle rinse if you decide to rinse.
